candidates.expected: NL3 requires the system's root-level initial pseudostate edge to enter HumanDrivingMode on power-on as the machine's default first entry, matching the plain, unconditional semantics of a UML initial-pseudostate transition ([*] -> HumanDrivingMode).

response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structural containment/entry defects, transition-group guard collisions, and cross-context contrasts using the exact source inventory, working contract macro mapping, and closed FCSTM/inspection facts. Key findings: (1) NL2/NL2-REGION are satisfied by AutonomousMode containing SubState1-3. (2) NL3's root-level initial entry to HumanDrivingMode is structurally satisfied by tr_0001/transition:line:28 mapping through the source macro, but the FCSTM-level pseudostate edge at line:28 carries a Power_On trigger and is flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/refuted by verify_facts, which is a genuine structural defect on the initial edge itself (an initial pseudostate transition should be unconditional per source semantics, matching a working-contract diagnostic W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING at composite root). (3) NL4/NL4-GUARD endpoints and guard are satisfied by transition:line:29 (HumanDrivingMode->AutonomousMode, guard/trigger _front_distance_10 correctly reflecting front_distance>10). (4) NL4.2 endpoint AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode exists at transition:line:26, but the trigger set required by NL (event=human steering cmd, guard=brake pressed and in(auto final)) does not match the actual guard R45RouteToken==7 with no triggers; the actual mechanism is a synthetic route-token relay rather than the literal conjunctive condition, which is a structural mismatch worth flagging as a guard/trigger gap (predicate-null W1) distinct from satisfied endpoint existence. (5) NL5 endpoint HumanDrivingMode->final exists (transition:line:30), and AutonomousMode->final also exists (transition:line:27) satisfying the derived NL5-DERIVED source-ambiguity contract. NL5-TERMINATION requires auditing whether reaching a state deemed 'final' can re-enter: AutonomousMode's power-off exit uses R45RouteToken==9 guard, which requires the token to be set from an inner SubState/FinalWait Power_Off transition first; a direct external Power_Off event on AutonomousMode itself has no consumer transition other than via child token-setting, meaning the sole path to actual final termination depends on nested indirection, which is contrastively consistent structurally, so no additional termination defect beyond what's already covered by the initial-entry issue. (6) auto final containment/declaration derived contracts NL4.2-DERIVED are satisfied via FinalWaittr_0005 (line:12) as a child of AutonomousMode, contained correctly, so omitted from candidates.

candidates.basis: fcstm_model text: AutonomousMode -> HumanDrivingMode : if [R45RouteToken == 7]; AutonomousMode -> [*] : if [R45RouteToken == 9]; FinalWaittr_0005 -> [*] on both human_steering_cmd(token=7) and Power_Off(token=9); inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions lines 23,24,26,27.
candidates.expected: On power off, the system must stably reach a final/terminal configuration without a live competing continuation back into operating behavior.
candidates.observed: AutonomousMode's only edges out of the composite are AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode (transition:line:26, guard R45RouteToken==7) and AutonomousMode->[*] (transition:line:27, guard R45RouteToken==9); reaching the final/[*] route requires the internal SubState/FinalWaittr_0005 machinery to have last set R45RouteToken=9, and FinalWaittr_0005 itself retains outgoing routes for both the human-steering event (token=7, re-entering HumanDrivingMode) and Power_Off (token=9, terminating), so the same shared completion state can route back into human driving mode instead of terminating depending on which event fires last.
candidates.reason: The contract requires stable termination reachable from the system on power off; the shared token-relay design co-locates the termination edge with a same-named completion carrier (FinalWaittr_0005/AutonomousMode) that also supports a full return-to-operation route, so the target ancestry does not exclusively and stably lead to completion without deterministic confirmation that no interleaving exists where a residual state permits the wrong route to be taken, and this ambiguity is exactly the kind of active-ancestor continuation this lens must flag even though endpoint transitions exist.
candidates.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: Since Power_Off specifically produces token=9 on every SubState/FinalWaittr_0005 exit, an actual Power_Off stimulus deterministically selects the AutonomousMode->[*] termination route; the re-entry route is only selected by the distinct human-steering-cmd event, so termination on power-off specifically may still be sound.
candidates.title: Power-off termination is not stable: AutonomousMode retains a live non-terminating continuation (R45RouteToken==7 route back to HumanDrivingMode) alongside the completion route

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability via the initial pseudostate, reachable event-consumer coverage for Power_On, stable termination for the power-off obligation, and the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode return group's guard/trigger semantics against the closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) the root initial edge [*]->HumanDrivingMode (transition:line:28) carries a spurious Power_On trigger, is marked reachable_from_initial=false, and is refuted by verify_facts initial-entry check, which both violates the NL3 initial_entry obligation and independently breaks reachable coverage of the declared Power_On event consumer (verify_facts event-consumer:Power_On refuted, reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); (2) the NL5/derived power-off termination contracts are satisfied structurally by exact edges to [*] from HumanDrivingMode and AutonomousMode, but AutonomousMode's completion path first requires internal SubState1->SubState2->SubState3->FinalWaittr_0005 progression and even FinalWaittr_0005 retains outgoing routes back into human_steering_cmd/Power_Off effects rather than a bare final state, and AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode (transition:line:26, guard R45RouteToken==7) provides a live continuation path competing with termination, so termination is not stably closed; (3) the NL4.2 return-transition trigger/guard set is structurally reshaped by the compiler into an effect-token relay (SubStateN -> [*] on the shared event, then AutonomousMode -> HumanDrivingMode gated on R45RouteToken==7) losing the explicit brake-pressed/auto-final conjunction as an atomic transition guard, which is evidence for the guard/triggerset contract rather than a new property.

candidate.observed: The closed FCSTM initial edge at transition:line:28 ([*] -> HumanDrivingMode) is annotated with trigger Power_On and is flagged by inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL ('An initial pseudostate transition carries a trigger or guard') and verify_facts check initial-entry:transition:line:28 with status=refuted (has_trigger=true). candidate.reason: NL3 establishes an exact root-owner initial-entry obligation targeting HumanDrivingMode.
